title: Coherent realization of inner anodyne maps
statement: Use simplicial sets, standard simplices, horns and weak homotopy equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and the subset-poset coherent realization $\mathfrak C$ of [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching]. An inner anodyne map is a member of the smallest class containing all isomorphisms and $\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ for $n\geq2$, $0<i<n$, and closed under arbitrary pushouts, small continuous transfinite compositions and arrow retracts. A simplicial functor is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence if it induces weak homotopy equivalences on every mapping simplicial set and an equivalence of categories after taking path components of mapping simplicial sets. For every inner anodyne map $u:A\to B$ of small simplicial sets, $\mathfrak C[u]$ is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence. There is no quasicategory hypothesis on $A$ or $B$.

source.place: Lemma 2.2.5.2 and its cubical proof, preceding the proof of Theorem 2.2.5.1; only the trivial-cofibration assertion for coherent inner horns and its saturation are used, not the coherent-nerve Quillen equivalence. No Stacks tag states this result. HTT reading copy is in the sandbox; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: The colimit formula of [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching] makes $\mathfrak C$ colimit preserving. Explicitly, for any small simplicial category $D$, put $N_D{}_r=\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathrm{sCat}}(\mathfrak C[\Delta^r],D)$ with operators given by precomposition. A functor $\mathfrak C[S]\to D$ is precisely a compatible choice of such a functor for each simplex of $S$, hence precisely a simplicial map $S\to N_D$. Applying this bijection to a colimit cocone shows directly that $\mathfrak C$ takes every small colimit cocone to a colimit cocone. It also preserves arrow retract diagrams, since these are functorial identities.

source.place: Section 1.1.5, paragraph preceding Example 1.1.5.9; Lemma 2.2.5.2, weak-saturation reduction.

proof.text: Fix $n\geq2$ and $0<i<n$. In degree $r$, the subset-poset model of [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching] identifies an arrow $a\to b$ with a flag $S_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq S_r\subseteq\{a,\ldots,b\}$ containing both endpoints. Apply [lem-coef-coherent-realization-bead-normal-form] to $\Delta^n$: its degree-$r$ category is free on beads. In this simplex model a bead is exactly a flag with $S_0=\{a,b\}$, supported on the face with vertex set $S_r$; its normalized final set is that whole face, as in the cited statement. The unique word factorization cuts the flag at successive vertices of $S_0$. For any union of faces $H\subseteq\Delta^n$, the same node's subcomplex-image clause identifies $\mathfrak C[H]$ with the free subcategory on the beads whose supporting simplex belongs to $H$. In particular, an indecomposable flag belongs exactly when its largest set lies in one of those faces, and any word belongs exactly when every bead does. This identification is simplicial: the cited operator clause acts on subset flags and then expresses the result as the unique bead word. Thus both the free-flag presentation and its compatibility with all simplicial operators are supplied by that node, without assuming that enriched colimits are degreewise colimits.

source.place: Definitions 5.1.1, 5.1.4 and 5.1.11, Proposition 5.1.12; specialization of the existing bead-normal-form statement to a simplex and its face subcomplexes, realizing the same flag route as HTT Lemma 2.2.5.2.

proof.text:
Apply the preceding presentation to $H=\Lambda_i^n$, the union of the faces omitting $k
eq i$ as defined in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. All objects occur. If $[a,b]
eq[0,n]$, some vertex outside $[a,b]$ differs from $i$ (the excluded singleton case would force $i$ to be an endpoint). Hence every flag from $a$ to $b$ already belongs to a face of $H$. For $(a,b)=(0,n)$, every decomposable flag is present, since its factors have proper endpoint intervals. These are precisely the flags for which some internal vertex belongs to $S_0$. An indecomposable flag is present exactly when $S_r$ omits some internal $k
eq i$. Identify the mapping cube with $Q=(\Delta^1)^{\{1,\ldots,n-1\}}$ using characteristic functions of subsets, as in [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching]. Membership in $S_0$ means a coordinate is constantly $1$, and omission from $S_r$ means it is constantly $0$. Consequently $\mathfrak C[H]$ agrees with $\mathfrak C[\Delta^n]$ except that its $(0,n)$ mapping set is
$$K= igcup_{j=1}^{n-1}\{t_j=1\}\ \cup\! igcup_{1\leq j\leq n-1,\ j
eq i}\{t_j=0\}\ \subseteq Q.$$
All compositions through an intermediate object land in the faces $t_j=1$ of $K$, by union composition. Thus adjoining $Q$ along $K$ at the single pair $(0,n)$ gives $\mathfrak C[\Delta^n]$; explicitly it is the pushout of $U(K)	o U(Q)$ of [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting], with its objects sent to $0,n$. There are no other new composites, because no nonidentity arrow enters $0$ or leaves $n$.

source.place: Lemma 2.2.5.2, both bullets and the two-object pushout; Proposition 1.1.5.10, missing-face cube; explicit determination of which face is absent.

proof.text:
Let $R=(\Delta^1)^{\{1,\ldots,n-1\}\setminus\{i\}}$ and let $\partial R$ be the union of its coordinate $0$- and $1$-faces, with $\partial R=\varnothing$ when $R=\Delta^0$. Up to reordering coordinates the map $K\hookrightarrow Q$ is
$$(\partial R\times\Delta^1)\amalg_{\partial R\times\{1\}}(R\times\{1\})\longrightarrow R\times\Delta^1.$$
The map $\partial R\hookrightarrow R$ is degreewise injective. The map $\{1\}\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$ is $\Lambda_1^1\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$; it has the left lifting property against every Kan fibration directly from that definition in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. The pushout-product theorem [lem-coef-sset-anodyne-pushout-product] therefore says that $K\hookrightarrow Q$ has the left lifting property against every Kan fibration. This argument includes $n=2$, where it is just the endpoint inclusion into the interval.

source.place: Lemma 2.2.5.2, final sentence (open-box inclusion is a trivial cofibration); explicit pushout-product justification.

proof.text: Use $J$, $J\text{-inj}$ and $J\text{-cof}$ from [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting]. In a lifting square with $\mathfrak C[H]\to\mathfrak C[\Delta^n]$ on the left and $p:E\to F$ in $J\text{-inj}$ on the right, the object choices are already fixed because the left map is the identity on objects. All mapping maps except $(0,n)$ are already fixed. The remaining square is $K\to E(e_0,e_n)$ over $Q\to F(pe_0,pe_n)$. The cited node states that $E(e_0,e_n)\to F(pe_0,pe_n)$ is a Kan fibration, so step 4 gives a filler. It respects every composition because on every face $t_j=1$ it agrees with the original map on $K$; these are all nonidentity compositions involving this mapping set, by step 3. It gives a simplicial functor filling the original square. Thus every coherent inner horn map is in $J\text{-cof}$, with no local Kan condition on $E,F$ and no condition that their object images be distinct.

source.place: Lemma 2.2.5.2, two-object pushout; Appendix A.3.2, horn generators; direct lifting argument in place of assuming the coherent-nerve Quillen theorem.

proof.text: A left lifting class such as $J\text{-cof}$ of [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting] contains isomorphisms and is closed under pushouts, small continuous transfinite compositions and arrow retracts. For a pushout square pull the lifting problem back to the original map and descend the filler by its universal property. Along an ordinal chain choose the filler successively extending the previous one; at a limit stage the compatible fillers give the required map from the colimit. For an arrow retract precompose and postcompose the filler with the retraction maps. By step 1, the class of simplicial maps $v$ with $\mathfrak C[v]\in J\text{-cof}$ has the same closure properties. Step 5 puts every inner horn in it. The defining minimality of the inner anodyne class in the statement therefore puts every inner anodyne $u$ in this inverse-image class.

source.place: Lemma 2.2.5.2, weak saturation, expanded from the lifting definition; Definition A.1.2.2.

proof.text: For the given inner anodyne $u$, step 6 gives $\mathfrak C[u]\in J\text{-cof}$. By [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting], every $J\text{-cof}$ map is an arrow retract of a $J\text{-cell}$ map. By [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-cell-stability], every such cell map is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence and that class is closed under retracts. It follows that $\mathfrak C[u]$ is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence, which gives both the mapping-set weak equivalences and the equivalence on $\pi_0$ required by the statement. The argument used no horn filling hypothesis on $A$ or $B$ and allows arbitrary small attaching diagrams and ordinal lengths.

source.place: Lemma 2.2.5.2, first paragraph and conclusion; Appendix A.3.2, horn-cell weak equivalences, supplied by the existing interval-cell-stability node.
